sections.title: Sound of letter A
paragraphs: The letter (A) /eɪ/ is called (A) /eɪ/. Its main sound is the vowel /æ/, heard in the word (apple) /æ.pəl/, which means apple. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter can make four different sounds.

sections.title: How to say letter A
paragraphs: Drop your jaw low and keep your tongue flat and forward. Push your voice through your throat to say the first vowel. For the next sound, glide your tongue smoothly from the middle up toward the roof. For the third sound, relax your mouth completely and let out a gentle puff. Open your mouth wide and pull your tongue back for the last sound.

sections.title: Spelling of letter A
paragraphs: In closed syllables, you say the sound /æ/, as in (cat) /kæt/. In open syllables or before a silent e, use the diphthong /eɪ/, like in (make) /meɪk/. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable, where the sound glides from the first to the second. In unstressed syllables, say the schwa /ə/, as in (about) /ə.baʊt/. Before the letter r or in special words, make the long sound /ɑː/, heard in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with letter A
paragraphs: Do not replace the vowel /æ/ with the vowel sound in bed. Open your mouth much wider and flatten your tongue forward. Do not use a short single vowel for the diphthong in words like day. Slide your tongue upward to finish the glide properly. Keep unstressed vowels weak instead of pronouncing them clearly.
